concept: FDE Portfolio Capstone: Northstar Support Operations
title: FDE Portfolio Capstone: Northstar Support Operations Checkpoint

questions.prompt: What is the first useful Northstar capstone increment?

options.label: A full autonomous refund platform before clarifying permissions.
A presentation without any reproducible workflow.
One authorized order-status workflow with evidence, failure states and a baseline.

questions.explanation: A bounded vertical slice provides end-to-end learning and measurable behavior. Excess scope and presentation-only work miss the delivery objective.

questions.prompt: Which test belongs in the capstone acceptance matrix?

options.label: The UI hides the admin button but the API permits the action.
Tenant A cannot obtain tenant B's ticket through the API, cache or model context.
Every tenant can see all records so the demo is easier.

questions.explanation: Isolation must cover actual access paths. Visibility controls alone do not enforce authorization, and broad demo access invalidates the requirement.

questions.prompt: A fake provider applies an action then raises a timeout. What must the capstone demonstrate?

options.label: Explicit uncertainty and reconciliation without blindly creating a second operation.
A fresh operation key on every retry.
A completed state invented from the fact that a request was sent.

questions.explanation: The fixture probes the ambiguous outcome boundary. New keys can duplicate work; sending a request does not prove completion.

questions.prompt: You timed your own synthetic workflow and saved five minutes. How should the portfolio describe it?

options.label: A company-wide savings claim without adoption data.
A local synthetic observation with workload and measurement limits.

questions.explanation: Evidence labels preserve credibility. Personal fixture timing is useful but does not establish real customer adoption or organization-wide impact.
